question.text: What is the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for handling stock exchange outages as prescribed by SEBI?

answer.text: The affected exchange must immediately inform SEBI and market participants; trading continues on unaffected exchanges; the affected exchange must try to restore operations and give 15 minutes notice before resuming
All exchanges must halt trading simultaneously if any one exchange faces an outage
There is no SOP — exchanges handle outages at their discretion without informing SEBI
Trading on all derivative segments is suspended for 24 hours when any exchange faces an outage

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SOP, the affected exchange informs SEBI immediately and informs participants/MIIs within about 15 minutes; unaffected segments and other exchanges continue trading; the affected exchange works to restore normalcy, gives 15 minutes notice before resumption, and extension rules apply to make up affected time. The Trap: Trading does not halt across all exchanges, the handling is not discretionary, and there is no blanket 24-hour suspension across derivative segments. Note: The SOP focuses on stock exchange outage handling. It is separate from the IRRA facility, which addresses disruption of trading services provided by a trading member.
